title: Clone Graph
description:
Given a reference of a node in a **connected undirected graph**, return a **deep copy** (clone) of the graph.

Each node in the graph contains a value (`val`) and a list of its neighbors (`neighbors`).

examples.explanation:
There are 4 nodes in the graph.
Node 1 connects to 2 and 4.
Node 2 connects to 1 and 3.
Node 3 connects to 2 and 4.
Node 4 connects to 1 and 3.

constraints: The number of nodes in the graph is in the range [0, 100].
Node.val is unique for each node.
There are no repeated edges and no self-loops in the graph.
hints: Use Breadth-First Search (BFS) with a queue and a hash map to map original nodes to their cloned counterparts.
For each neighbor of the current node, if it has not been cloned yet, clone it and push it to the queue.

solutions.explanation: Traverse the graph using BFS. Use a Hash Map to record visited nodes and store mapping from original node to cloned node.

dryRunSteps.explanation: Initialize queue with Node 1 and clone Node 1 into the hash map.
Dequeue Node 1. Inspect neighbors [2, 4]. Clone Node 2 and Node 4, then enqueue both.
Dequeue Node 2. Inspect neighbor Node 3. Clone Node 3 and add to queue.
Dequeue Node 4. Neighbors [1, 3] are already cloned. Link cloned edges.
Queue is empty. All nodes and edges copied. Return cloned Node 1.

realWorldUseCases.description: Deep-copying layers, vectors, and component hierarchy using graph BFS cloning.
